quoted_clause: the economic lesson (diminishing cost of a marginal host once fixed costs dominate) is sound
observed: The phrase 'diminishing cost of a marginal host' most naturally parses as the marginal host's own cost diminishing, which would contradict §1's explicit statement that 'The marginal cost of each added host, however, is roughly constant in this model.' The benign reading (average cost per request declining through amortization of fixed costs) is supported by §1's 'The economic lever is amortizing the fixed term, not the marginal one,' but the parenthetical phrasing is ambiguous enough to be read as claiming falling marginal cost.
evidence: §1 states: 'The marginal cost of each added host, however, is roughly constant in this model — one host buys ~2.0 req/s at ~$20/hr, so the marginal cost stays near ~$10 per req/s per hour … The economic lever is amortizing the fixed term, not the marginal one.' §3 then says 'the economic lesson (diminishing cost of a marginal host once fixed costs dominate) is sound.' Under the amortization reading the two are consistent; under the literal reading of 'diminishing cost of a marginal host' they appear contradictory.
root_cause: Ambiguous phrasing: 'diminishing cost of a marginal host' can be parsed as (a) the marginal host's cost diminishes [contradicts §1] or (b) the average cost per request diminishes due to adding a marginal host [consistent with §1].
correction: Rewrite the parenthetical to disambiguate, e.g., 'the economic lesson (average cost per request declines as fixed costs amortize across more requests) is sound' or 'the economic lesson (diminishing average cost per request once fixed costs dominate) is sound.'
acceptance_test: A reader unfamiliar with §1 should not be able to parse the §3 parenthetical as claiming marginal cost diminishes.

quoted_clause: so the ~93% headroom is a property of the linear-only convention, not of the hardware
observed: The phrase '~93% headroom' conflates utilization with headroom. The preceding sentences establish that prefill runs at ~93% of the ceiling (93% utilization, 7% headroom). '93% headroom' most naturally reads as 93% of capacity being available (i.e., only 7% used), which is the inverse of the intended meaning.
evidence: The same section states: 'The ratio is 18,400 ÷ 19,780 ≈ 93% under case (i)' and 'Prefill must run at ~93% of the idealized prefill ceiling under case (i).' These establish 93% as utilization. The headroom is 100% − 93% = 7%. The phrase '~93% headroom' inverts this.
root_cause: Terminology slip: 'headroom' is used where 'utilization' (or '7% headroom') is meant.
correction: Rewrite as 'so the ~7% headroom under case (i) is a property of the linear-only convention' or 'so the ~93% utilization under case (i) is a property of the linear-only convention.'
acceptance_test: The sentence should not be parseable as claiming 93% of the prefill ceiling is unused.

quoted_clause: ~10 requests/s average ... at the canonical 6.24M requests/mo
observed: 10 rps × 86,400 s/day × 30 days = 25,920,000 ≈ 25.92M requests/mo, but the ADR uses 6.24M requests/mo — a 4.15× discrepancy. The chunk presents both as canonical without stating any operating-window basis (business hours, duty cycle) that would reconcile them.
evidence: 10 × 86,400 × 30 = 25,920,000. 25.92M ÷ 6.24M = 4.154. Step 2 establishes ~10 rps average; the ADR (§6) uses 6.24M for all $/1K divisions ($155.8K/6.24M×1000 = $24.97 ✓, $87.6K/6.24M×1000 = $14.04 ✓, $129.8K/6.24M×1000 = $20.80 ✓ — internally consistent with 6.24M but not with 10 rps sustained). No basis difference is stated in this chunk.
root_cause: Volume-basis mismatch: the canonical traffic rate (10 rps) and the canonical monthly volume (6.24M) are inconsistent unless an unstated operating-window basis applies. The chunk does not explain the basis, so a reader computing 10 × 86,400 × 30 gets 25.92M and finds a contradiction with the ADR's 6.24M.
correction: State the operating-window basis explicitly where 6.24M is introduced (e.g., '6.24M/mo at 10 rps during 8 h × 22 d business hours') or reconcile 10 rps with 6.24M in a single sentence in this chunk.
acceptance_test: A reader computing 10 rps × 86,400 × 30 arrives at the same monthly volume used in the ADR, or the chunk states the basis that yields 6.24M.

quoted_clause: the quantities that issue from it are the evidence [1P]/[2°]/(to be verified) that every following chapter trades on
observed: The quantities derived from the canonical loop are labeled [ASSUMPTION] and [DERIVED] throughout Steps 1–4 and Table 22-1, but Step 5 tags them as [1P]/[2°]/(to be verified). [1P] means first-party measured; none of the loop quantities (9,200 tokens, 300 tokens, 10 rps, derived throughputs/FLOPs) are first-party measurements.
evidence: Step 1: '[canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]'; Step 2: '[canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]'; Steps 3–4 and Table 22-1: '[DERIVED]' and '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]'. No quantity in the loop carries [1P]. The canonical evidence-label vocabulary is [CANONICAL] [DERIVED] [ILLUSTRATIVE] [ASSUMPTION] [1P] [HYPOTHESIS]; [2°] is not in that list.
root_cause: Evidence-label mismatch: Step 5 applies [1P]/[2°] tags that do not match the labels assigned to the same quantities in Steps 1–4 and Table 22-1.
correction: Replace '[1P]/[2°]/(to be verified)' with the actual labels the quantities carry (e.g., '[ASSUMPTION]/[DERIVED]/(to be verified)'), or clarify that [1P]/[2°] refers to downstream evidence types rather than the loop quantities themselves.
acceptance_test: Every evidence tag in Step 5 matches the tag assigned to the same quantity in Steps 1–4 or Table 22-1.

quoted_clause: These are the book's [canonical scenario] inputs (Ch 4, Table 4-2) ... From the unit-and-token work of Ch 1 alone, the architect can already state the hard numbers
observed: Step 1 attributes the canonical token counts (~9,200 input, ~300 output) to Ch 4, Table 4-2. The end-of-chapter mini-case attributes the same numbers to 'the unit-and-token work of Ch 1.'
evidence: Step 1: '(Ch 4, Table 4-2)'. Mini-case: 'From the unit-and-token work of Ch 1 alone, the architect can already state the hard numbers: each request carries ~9.2K input tokens and ~300 output tokens.'
root_cause: Cross-chapter reference inconsistency: the same canonical values are attributed to two different chapters within the same chunk.
correction: Align the mini-case reference with Step 1 (Ch 4) or clarify that Ch 1 introduces the method and Ch 4 tabulates the specific values.
acceptance_test: The chapter reference for the canonical token counts is consistent between Step 1 and the mini-case.

quoted_clause: Most AI projects fail in requirements, not in technology.
observed: This is an empirical claim presented as established fact without an evidence label ([HYPOTHESIS], [1P], etc.).
evidence: The sentence appears in the Concept section with no evidence tag. Per the evidence-label vocabulary, empirical claims require a scope label.
root_cause: Missing evidence label on an empirical claim.
correction: Add an evidence label, e.g., '[HYPOTHESIS]' or '[1P]' if supported by a cited source.
acceptance_test: Every empirical claim in Ch 23 §1 carries an evidence label from the canonical vocabulary.

quoted_clause: the inputs Ch1-16 consume: traffic feeds capacity (Ch17)
observed: The text claims the six bounds are 'exactly the inputs Ch1-16 consume' but the first item in the enumerated list cites Ch17, which is outside the stated range Ch1-16.
evidence: Direct reading: 'Ch1-16' defines a range ending at Ch16; the enumerated consumers are (Ch17), (Ch7), (Ch5), (Ch11), (Ch16), (Ch13). Five of six fall within Ch1-16; Ch17 exceeds it.
root_cause: Off-by-one error in the chapter range — the upper bound should include Ch17.
correction: Change 'Ch1-16' to 'Ch1-17' (or the correct upper bound encompassing all six cited chapters).
acceptance_test: Re-read the clause; verify every chapter cited in the enumerated list falls within the stated range.

quoted_clause: five question gates (problem, success, data, constraints, scope)
observed: The figure caption states 'five question gates' listing five items, but the figure specification comment in the same chunk states 'six labeled question gates.' The chapter text consistently refers to 'six numbers' / 'six bounds.'
evidence: Caption: 'broad ask → five question gates (problem, success, data, constraints, scope) → confirmed bounds.' Figure spec: 'six labeled question gates narrow it.' Direct contradiction: 5 vs 6.
root_cause: Caption and figure specification disagree on the gate count. Either the caption undercounts or the spec overcounts; the rendered figure must be inspected to determine which is correct.
correction: Reconcile caption and spec to agree on the gate count and names. If the figure shows six gates, update the caption from 'five' to 'six' and adjust the listed gate names; if five, update the spec.
acceptance_test: Vision stage: compare the rendered figure's gate count and labels against the caption text; verify they match.

observed: Section 3.3 presents multiple derived quantities (51.5 PFLOP/s, 6.5 hosts, 16.3 hosts, ≈4.8 KV-residency hosts, ~45% lower cost, ~1.6 nodes) without explicit bracketed evidence labels ([DERIVED]), whereas adjacent Sections 3.1 and 3.2 label their derived quantities with [ILLUSTRATIVE] and/or [DERIVED] tags.
evidence: Section 3.1: 'PIES = 217 [ILLUSTRATIVE]'. Section 3.2: '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] — null-model uniform-retrieval baseline.' Section 3.3: no bracketed labels on any derived number; scope provided only through prose caveats ('theoretical compute floor', 'not a production sizing result').
root_cause: Inconsistent application of the evidence-label vocabulary across sibling sections within the same chapter.
correction: Add [DERIVED] (and [CANONICAL] where inputs are canonical scenario values) labels to the derived quantities in Section 3.3, consistent with Sections 3.1–3.2.
